WORKED EXAMPLE: VERTICAL SUMMATION

runs.text: Horizontal axis: community fireworks displays per summer; vertical axis: marginal benefit / cost in thousands of dollars per display. Dashed North MB falls from 50 at zero displays to 30 at four; dashed South MB falls from 40 to 20 at four and reaches zero at eight. Solid MSB is their vertical sum: 90 at zero and 50 at four. Horizontal MC is 50. At four displays, guides mark North 30, South 20 and the MSB-MC intersection at 50. MSB then falls to zero at ten displays.

transcript.sourceText: At four community fireworks displays, North's marginal benefit is $30,000 and South's is $20,000. Because both communities consume the same shared quantity, MSB is the vertical sum: $50,000. MC is also $50,000, so four displays are efficient. Summing quantities horizontally would be incorrect.

Summing quantities horizontally would be incorrect.
